newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua willing to return ex-dictator's property.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua willing to return ex-dictator's property.

text.p: In a move bound to enrage the Nicaraguan left, President Arnoldo Aleman on Friday invited the family of former dictator Anastasio Somoza to return and go to court to recover its confiscated properties.
"The Somoza family should come here to argue its case about the properties in court. Let's see what the courts say to the Somozas," Aleman told reporters.
Somoza, whose family ruled Nicaragua with an iron fist for 43 years, was toppled in the 1979 Sandinista revolution and the family's many properties were confiscated by the revolutionary government.
Somoza was gunned down in the streets of Asuncion, Paraguay on Sept. 19, 1981.
Aleman said it was up to the courts not him to decide whether Somoza's confiscated properties were returned to his family, who live in exile in the United States.
The properties include an opulent mansion in run-down Managua that has since been turned into a sport institute, as well as beachfront homes that have become tourist sites.
The Sandinistas, who governed from 1979 to 1990, angrily accused Aleman of sympathising with Somoza during a bitter election contest that brought him to power in January.
Aleman argued that the return of properties confiscated by the Sandinistas while in office was essential for restoring confidence in private property rights and the rule of law.
